role: Interface of a world's save directory (SaveHandler, AnvilSaveHandler): level.dat read and write, the session lock, the chunk loader for a dimension, player data and the data/ folder for MapStorage files.
scope_reason: Saving and reloading a world is part of the played game (checkpoints, play-reload tapes); the interface itself has no behavior. The save-writing side is deferred: native never writes save files; Java writes every checkpoint (product decision, not a gap for the GPU or the golden chain; triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md). The read side is a real item (B2).

notes: Interface only; behavior lives in SaveHandler and AnvilSaveHandler. region.c's header says it serves the checkpoint --from start; serverreplay.c calls region_enumerate and region_load_chunk. The disk half is n/a (lane/idxworld): every save this game makes is the oracle's (a checkpoint's save, session.sh's Save and Quit through Java: AGENTS.md 'Playing a full game'), and the native engine reads what it wrote (region.c for the overworld's region files, the snapshot's saved chunks for DIM-1 and DIM1, structures.json, villages.nbt, worldinfo.nbt, player_server.nbt); writing those files natively is the deferred product work of the 2026-09-25 triage (SPEC.md NEXT, '11 deferred save-writing'; out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md, 'Deferred, not noise'). Within a session nothing reads a save back: an unloaded chunk waits whole in the in-memory region store (sr_store_chunk) with what writeChunkToNBT keeps of it (the entities it saves, in section order; the pending ticks relative to the world time), and a reload restores exactly that (the persist-* and play-reload recordings).
